newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia sees slight '97 dilution from deal.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia sees slight '97 dilution from deal.

text.p: Wachovia Corp said it expects its planned acquisition of Jefferson Bankshares Inc to be one percent dilutive in 1997 based on generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
On a per share basis, the $542 million acquisition will have no impact on earnings for the year, said chief financial officer Robert McCoy.
Speaking to reporters in a telephone conference call, McCoy also said the acquisition will include $320 million to $340 million of goodwill to be amortized over 20 years.

Wachovia chief executive Leslie Baker said the transaction is expected to generate $18 million per year in cost savings. The company also said the acquisition will result in a $19 million charge against earnings, but timing for the charge has not yet been determined.

Baker also said Wachovia will pursue other acquisitions in the region, noting that Maryland is an attractive area. He also said Wachovia would consider some branches being sold by Signet Banking Corp.
"We are very interested in growing our presence in the Southeast. You can look for us to be examining other specific markets in the months and years ahead," he said.
Jefferson chief executive Kenton McCartney said he approached Baker two weeks ago about a transaction following an intensive study by the Jefferson board.

McCoy also said that Wachovia will continue its existing share buyback program. The company bought back 2.6 million shares in the first quarter and is likely to repurchase the same amount in the second quarter, he said.
